monuments.name: Golden Gate Bridge
monuments.architect: 1,280m Art Deco Stepped-Tower Suspension Bridge in International Orange (Joseph Strauss, Charles Ellis & Irving Morrow, 1937)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 1,280m Art Deco Stepped-Tower Suspension Bridge in International Orange (Joseph Strauss, Charles Ellis & Irving Morrow, 1937)
monuments.fact: Opened on May 27, 1937 across the mile-wide tidal strait where San Francisco Bay meets the Pacific Ocean; architect Irving Morrow championed its signature International Orange finish and Art Deco stepped tower setbacks.

monuments.name: Transamerica Pyramid
monuments.architect: 260m White Quartz Precast Concrete Four-Sided Pyramid, Elevator Wings & Glass Beacon Crown (William Pereira, 1972)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 260m White Quartz Precast Concrete Four-Sided Pyramid, Elevator Wings & Glass Beacon Crown (William Pereira, 1972)
monuments.fact: Designed by William Pereira on the historic site of the 1853 Montgomery Block so its tapered pyramidal silhouette would let sunlight reach Columbus Avenue and Redwood Park below.

monuments.name: Coit Tower (Telegraph Hill)
monuments.architect: 64m Fluted White Concrete Art Deco Belvedere Column & WPA Fresco Rotunda (Arthur Brown Jr., 1933)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 64m Fluted White Concrete Art Deco Belvedere Column & WPA Fresco Rotunda (Arthur Brown Jr., 1933)
monuments.fact: Funded by eccentric bequest from Lillie Hitchcock Coit—patroness of San Francisco’s volunteer firefighters—and designed by City Hall architect Arthur Brown Jr. in 1933 with 27 New Deal frescoes painted inside its base.

monuments.name: San Francisco Ferry Building & Clock Tower
monuments.localName: San Francisco Ferry Building & Clock Tower
monuments.architect: 201m Beaux-Arts Colusa Sandstone Nave & 75m Seville Giralda Clock Tower (A. Page Brown, 1898)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 201m Beaux-Arts Colusa Sandstone Nave & 75m Seville Giralda Clock Tower (A. Page Brown, 1898)
monuments.fact: Standing at the foot of Market Street since 1898, A. Page Brown’s 75-meter clock tower survived both the 1906 earthquake and the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake—after which the elevated Embarcadero Freeway was torn down to restore its grand plaza.

monuments.name: Palace of Fine Arts Rotunda
monuments.architect: Beaux-Arts Classical Rotunda Dome, Corinthian Peristyle & Lagoon (Bernard Maybeck, 1915 / Rebuilt in Concrete 1965)
monuments.architecturalStyle: Beaux-Arts Classical Rotunda Dome, Corinthian Peristyle & Lagoon (Bernard Maybeck, 1915 / Rebuilt in Concrete 1965)
monuments.fact: Created by architect Bernard Maybeck for the 1915 Panama-Pacific International Exposition celebrating San Francisco’s rebirth after the 1906 earthquake and fire, evoking a romantic Roman ruin reflected in a tranquil swan lagoon.

monuments.name: Salesforce Tower & Transit Center
monuments.architect: 326.5m Tapered Glass & Brushed-Aluminum Obelisk Skyscraper & Rooftop Gondola Park (César Pelli, 2018)

monuments.fact: San Francisco’s tallest skyscraper (1,070 ft), anchored by 42 foundation piles driven 310 feet into Franciscan bedrock beside the four-block rooftop botanical park of the Salesforce Transit Center.

monuments.architecturalStyle: Six Queen Anne Victorian Rowhouses with Polychrome Gingerbread Gables & Bay Windows (Matthew Kavanaugh, 1892–1896)
monuments.fact: Built between 1892 and 1896 by developer Matthew Kavanaugh at 710–720 Steiner Street, these six Queen Anne Victorians survived the 1906 fire because the dynamite firebreak stopped at Van Ness Avenue.

monuments.name: Alcatraz Island Lighthouse & Cellhouse ("The Rock")
monuments.architect: Sandstone Bay Island, 1909 Octagonal Concrete Lighthouse, Water Tower & 1912 Federal Cellhouse
monuments.architecturalStyle: Sandstone Bay Island, 1909 Octagonal Concrete Lighthouse, Water Tower & 1912 Federal Cellhouse
monuments.fact: Home to the West Coast’s first lighthouse (1854, rebuilt 1909 after the 1906 earthquake), a Civil War fortress, the 1934–1963 Federal Penitentiary, and the historic 1969–1971 Occupation by the Indians of All Tribes.
